A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conformal super-resolution study. Their complete main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original Liu4K/SinSR evaluations, data-leakage and smoothing analyses, and DDColor colorization examples in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds DIV2K distribution-shift results in Table 2 and additional colorization masks in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The calibration equations, variance and smoothing constructions, similarity metrics and model usage are retained. Algorithm 1 corrects inconsistent threshold-variable notation to T_i without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on DIV2K natural images using calibration transferred from Liu4K, extending coverage to a different evaluation distribution. The existing super-resolution and colorization tasks remain.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain trusting the whole image, Angelopoulos et al. (2022b), and Kutiel et al. (2023). The revised interval-width visualization retains the same baseline; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new shift experiment applies Liu4K calibration to 100 DIV2K validation images at alpha values 0.075, 0.100 and 0.125. Figure 7 expands colorization evaluation from alpha 0.1 to 0.0875, 0.1 and 0.125. Existing Liu4K/SinSR settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a robustness test involving different calibration and evaluation distributions, while Figure 7 adds qualitative sensitivity to the fidelity level in colorization. The existing data-leakage and smoothing analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting and plotted uncertainty bands are retained. Table 2 follows the same reporting practice, without adding or revising repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained quantitative plots are unchanged. Table 2 adds shifted-data PSNR results, including 13.28 ± 7.30 for semantic masking at alpha 0.1 versus 11.73 ± 0.39 without masking. Figure 7 adds colorization outcomes at two additional fidelity levels.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 2.1, Propositions 3.1–3.2, Appendix A proofs and Appendix B counterexample are retained. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation or guarantee is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims concerning black-box conformal masks, fidelity and PSNR guarantees, data-leakage robustness and smoothing benefits. The added caveats clarify applicability without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses guarantees failing under distribution shift, the computational cost of multiple generations, and potential societal harms. Appendix E expands the argument against quantitative baseline comparisons and claims tighter confidence regions using an existing mask-size result.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces the redactedURL placeholder with an explicit GitHub repository address. Appendix C clarifies threshold references in Algorithm 1. The hardware, base-model and preprocessing disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, and approaches by Nehme et al. and Adapa et al., distinguishing them by their lack of formal guarantees. DIV2K references and further positioning against the retained baselines are also added.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization remain stable. v3 adds localized related-work, limitations and impact discussion, introduces Appendices D–E, and relabels colorization as Appendix F. It also updates the publication header and leaves a Section 4 sentence unfinished at 'doing no uncertainty'.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 replace unmasked predictions with pixel-error maps. The baseline comparison moves from Figure 6 to Figure 5 and replaces lower/upper images with interval-width heatmaps and error maps. Figure 7 becomes a three-alpha comparison, and Table 2 is added within the retained page format.

improvement.justification: The added shift test, explicit applicability and computation limits, more informative visual comparisons, and disclosed code address provide a limited net improvement. Some new interpretations remain overstated: Appendix E supplies no baseline metrics for its tighter-region claim, and Table 2's averages do not establish its claimed pointwise PSNR control.
